title: Smt integrity
description: The integrity document of SmtRun (the blob Smt.Integrity hands out): what the server did with what the nodes returned, in counts. Copies of a problem are compared by the digest of their rows and by nothing else; a copy is a lie only when it differs from the settled answer of the others; a model the server's evaluator calls failed accuses nobody by itself, and when the machines agree on it the problem is counted as a disagreement between the evaluator and the solver, each such problem by its index. No machine and no package is named.

copies_made.description: Answers taken, every round together: copies of a problem's row that are statements about it (a row of a fault of its node is not).

compared.description: Problems first ruled on two answers or more: the first fan-out's, with the repair round's for a problem it sent out again and answered (the lone answer of the first fan-out is compared with them by digest).

agreements.description: Of those, problems whose answers all gave one digest.

disagreements.description: Of those, problems whose answers gave more than one digest.

one_copy.description: Problems whose answer rests on one machine: one answer, or a lone answer of the first fan-out and a lone answer of the repair round with the same digest (two fan-outs may place them on one machine). A problem whose package was not sampled is one of them.

unsat_one_copy.description: Of those, problems answered unsat: nothing beyond that machine vouches for them.

disputes.description: Problems that went to three more machines.

disputes_resolved.description: Disputes a majority of the three settled.

disputed.description: Disputes that stand: rows with status disputed.

dispute_causes.description: Why the disputes went: the copies' digests differed; the evaluator called the model of the copies failed; more answers to the problem's package came back than were asked for.

lies.description: Answers that differ from the settled answer of the others: a lie was found in each.

problems_with_lies.description: Problems a lie was found in.

failed_models.description: Answers, every round together, whose model the evaluator called failed.

evaluator_solver_disagreements.description: Problems the machines agree on and the evaluator calls failed (settled_by agreement). No machine is counted as lying for them. Each is listed below by its index.

repairs.description: Problems the repair round sent out once more, every package of it to two machines: those without an answer from the first fan-out (sampled or not), and those of a package the first fan-out asked for twice that came back with fewer than two answers.

repairs_by_reason.description: The repairs by what the first fan-out said of the problem: for a problem without an answer, a node's fault code of its package, the code of a row of a fault of the node, the reason its package's result was refused, or no_answer; copies_short for a problem of a package asked for twice that came back with one answer.

no_result.description: Problems left without a result: rows with status no_result.

no_result_by_reason.description: The same by what the nodes said last.

rejected_results.description: Result packages the server refused, every round and reason together.

rejected.description: The refused result packages by reason. A refused package fails that package and not the run.

unknown_ticket.description: A result under a ticket the fan-out did not give out.

duplicate.description: The same result blob returned again.

unreadable.description: Not a package of results this version reads, not the bytes its reference names, or damaged.

content.description: Does not hold exactly the rows of its package (one missing, foreign or twice), or holds a row a node may not give: another ticket, another problem's id, hash or query, another controller version or platform, a word no row has, counts of models or values a session does not give, or a digest that is not its own.

surplus.description: More results under one ticket than copies were asked for, in the dispute round: which is the answer cannot be told, so none is taken. (In the first fan-out and the repair round such a ticket is kept, and its problems go to a dispute.)

node_faults.description: Packages a node said it could not work on (a fault code and no rows), every round together. Their problems have no answer from that node.

sampling_rate.description: The share of the packages the run asked to solve on two machines, as the script stated it to Smt.Settle; null when it did not.

sampling.description: Whether the sampling that was asked for happened; the same word as in the report: as_asked when every problem with an answer of a package asked for twice ended with two answers of one fan-out (the first, or the repair round that sent it out again) and as many such packages came back as the rate asks for; short otherwise.

unanswered_packages.description: The sum of unanswered over the fan-outs.

evaluator_solver_disagreements.description: Every problem the machines agree on and the evaluator calls failed, loudly: its index, the evaluator's reason and its detail.

fan_outs.description: One record a fan-out the script ran, in the order they ran: what it was asked for and what came back, counted in packages.

copies.description: The answers a selected package was asked for: 2 where a share is sampled and in the repair round (every package of it; a repair round of controllers before 0.4.0 without sampling asked for 1), 3 in a dispute.

selected.description: The packages asked for that many answers; null when the script did not state its rate.

complete.description: The packages that came back with that many taken answers, or more.

unanswered.description: The packages no taken answer came back for.
